title: GroundingProfile
description: An operator's declaration of the EVIDENCE ENVELOPE one workspace's agents answer inside: which identifiers count as references, what the answer may assert about a resolved record, and what a conclusion of a declared class must show before it may be rendered. OGR 1.7 (draft). CONFIGURATION, NOT WIRE: a profile is held by the runtime and resolved by agent_workspace; it MUST NOT appear in a GuardEvent and a runtime MUST NOT accept one from a producer. It is evaluated against a RECORD PROVIDER whose credential is the runtime's. An absent part checks nothing, and a workspace with no profile has no declared envelope. See specification/grounding.md.

profile.description: The profile's name. Named in the finding's `detector` ('grounding:<name>@<provider>') so a finding is traceable to the document that produced it.

version.description: OPTIONAL operator-chosen revision label, recorded with findings so a decision can be replayed against the envelope in force.

workspace.description: The workspace whose policy set this profile belongs to. Resolution is the runtime's; this documents the intended binding and is not an assertion a producer may make.

domain.description: A LABEL for the vertical this profile serves ('intellectual-property', 'life-sciences'). It is not a taxonomy axis and never appears in a category id: every finding maps onto the neutral safety.hallucination.* / safety.unsafe_advice.* leaves.

provider.description: OPTIONAL non-secret NAME of the record provider this profile expects ('epo-ops', 'clinicaltrials-gov', a vendor). Advisory; the runtime holds the credential and makes the lookups. MUST NOT be an address and MUST NOT carry a credential.

on_violation.description: The default outcome for a grounding finding. `flag` — an allow carrying the finding — is the default, unlike the mandate's: an epistemic guardrail's usual remedy is that the answer should say less, not that it should not exist.

outcomes.description: Per-leaf override of on_violation. The seed profiles set safety.hallucination.citation to `block`: nothing downstream can be built on a fabricated record.

references.description: WHAT THE ANSWER POINTS AT: the identifier grammars of the domain. Exactly one of `pattern` (a regex over the text) or `lexicon` (entity linking by the provider's name dictionary) per entry.

type.description: The record type the provider is asked for: 'patent', 'clinical_trial', 'drug', 'doi', 'case'.

pattern.description: Regex recognising a surface form of the identifier.

lexicon.description: Link by the provider's name dictionary instead of a grammar. ⚠️ A lexicon cannot see an INVENTED name; that case is a judge's.

normalize.description: How a surface form becomes a provider key.

strip.description: Regex of characters removed anywhere (whitespace, thousands separators, slashes).

strip_suffix.description: Regex removed from the end (a kind code such as B2 / A1, trailing punctuation).

provider_attributes.description: The record attributes this profile reads — what a provider must be able to answer to serve it. Documents the provider contract; neutral as to who serves it.

assertions.description: WHAT THE ANSWER SAYS ABOUT A RECORD: a text pattern that asserts an attribute value, compared against the resolved record of the nearest reference in its sentence. A contradiction is safety.hallucination.attribute.

rule.description: The domain rule this implements (OG-IP-003, OG-LS-002). Documentation, not an id the taxonomy registers.

reference.description: The reference type the assertion is about.

attribute.description: Dotted path into the record; may cite a capture group ('approvals.$1.status').

value.description: The asserted value; may cite a capture group ('$1').

absent.description: What an attribute the record does not carry means. `unjudged`: the provider did not say. `mismatch`: the attribute is CLOSED-WORLD — the provider enumerates every value that exists (a drug's approvals), so absence is a contradiction.

fields.description: WHAT THE ANSWER MUST SHOW: the evidence fields a conclusion may require. Exactly one of `pattern` (present in the text) or `resolved` (a count of references of a type the provider resolved).

missing.description: The leaf emitted when a conclusion requires this field and the answer lacks it.

conclusions.description: BEFORE IT MAY CONCLUDE: the conclusion classes of the domain, each with the envelope it requires and the forms of words that render it as decided.

verifiability.description: An honest label: `record` is checked against a provider, `structural` from the text alone, `judgment` needs a model judge or a person. A runtime MUST NOT implement a `judgment` rule by lexicon and report it as judged.

cues.description: Regexes whose match means the answer is rendering this class of conclusion.

determination.description: Regexes matching the DECIDED form — 'infringes', 'is invalid', 'is effective'. A match is safety.unsafe_advice.overreach regardless of how complete the envelope is.

requires.description: Field ids that must be present; each missing one emits the field's `missing` leaf.
